name_reason: Name follows the fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and accurately reflects the body: it busy-waits until the BIOS DOS tick counter at linear 0x46C (mem[0x40:6C], 18.2 Hz) has advanced by at least n_ticks since the cached reference. No Ghidra address residue (the '_n_' is the parameter-count descriptor, not a hex address). Sibling fd2_wait_one_bios_tick shares the same naming pattern.
purpose: Busy-wait spin loop that blocks until the BIOS DOS tick counter (linear 0x46C, ~55ms per tick at 18.2 Hz) has advanced by at least n_ticks; the project's coarse frame-pacing / animation-timing primitive.
logic_summary: Caches the current BIOS tick (sign-extended 16-bit read, MOVSX) into private state data_fd2_engine_wait_n_bios_ticks_last_seen, then spins: each iteration recomputes elapsed = (int16)((uint16)tick - (uint16)last_seen) (16-bit subtract truncated then sign-extended, reproducing asm SUB/TEST/JGE), adds 0x10000 if negative to handle 16-bit wrap, and loops while elapsed < n_ticks. On exit it refreshes the cached reference with another sign-extended read so the next call measures from this moment. The initial cache-store makes the cached reference == current tick at entry, so elapsed starts at 0. (__CHK(4) is the Watcom stack-probe prologue, not game logic.)

params.name: n_ticks
params.semantics: Number of BIOS ticks (~55ms each) to wait. Common call values: 1 (~55ms, one frame), 2 (~110ms, general animation pacing), 6 (~330ms, longer holds). Passed in EDX from [ESP+4]; compared signed against the wrapped elapsed count.
params.reason: Name precisely describes the value (count of BIOS ticks to wait) and carries no address residue. Matches caller usage across 96 call sites.

returns.semantics: No return value; pure delay side effect plus update of the private last-seen cache.

reads_globals: BIOS_TICK_WORD/BIOS_TICK_COUNT (linear 0x46C BIOS DOS tick counter; FD2_REPLAY build substitutes fd2_replay_tick())
data_fd2_engine_wait_n_bios_ticks_last_seen (0x53A2C, private cache read in the elapsed computation)
writes_globals: data_fd2_engine_wait_n_bios_ticks_last_seen (0x53A2C, private cache; written at entry and at exit)
comment_original_issue: Source comment block (lines 68-82) was accurate and concise, but contained two non-ASCII em-dashes (U+2014) at the lines describing the sign-extend behavior and the Ghidra decompiler bug, violating the ASCII-only rule for code comments.
notes: Verified against disassembly @ 0x17aa9: MOVSX word ptr [0x46C] -> MOV [0x53A2C] (sign-extended 16-bit cache-stores at 0x17abc/0x17ac9 and 0x17ae4/0x17ae7); SUB EAX,[0x53A2C] confirms the Ghidra decompile artifact (_DAT_0000046c - _DAT_0000046c) actually reads the cached last_seen; ADD EAX,0x10000 is the 16-bit wrap fixup; CMP EAX,EDX / JL is the loop condition. consts.h confirms BIOS_TICK_WORD=(volatile uint16*)0x46C and BIOS_TICK_COUNT=(volatile uint32*)0x46C with FD2_REPLAY variants calling fd2_replay_tick(). xref count = exactly 96 call sites across 43 distinct caller functions (animation/cutscene/combat/chapter-event/timing code); source comment's '96 callers' uses the file's call-site convention (cf. line 102 '1 caller'), left unchanged. Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent with the refined source understanding (its em-dashes are allowed in plate text), so plate untouched. Only the two em-dashes in the src comment were changed to '--'; no logic/type/signature touched.
